I've been farming this land in Quzhou for four decades. I know this soil, I know the rainfall patterns, I know what sells at market and what feeds my family. With 200 mu and well access, I have more flexibility than most of my neighbors.

**My thinking:**

Wheat and maize are my foundation — the classic Hebei rotation. I'll put 80 mu into winter wheat this October, and those same fields flip to summer maize in June after harvest. That's my core 80 mu doing double duty all year. I've done this rotation so long I know exactly how much urea to put down and when.

Squash is my listed cropping system and my cash earner. I'll dedicate 25 mu to it in spring. With 40 years here I know squash loves a deep-ploughed bed and needs more water than anything else I grow. Powdery mildew is always a threat so I spray preventatively — I've lost squash to it before when I waited.

Millet takes the remaining 15 mu. It's not glamorous but it's drought-tolerant as a backup if the well has issues mid-summer, and I can always move it locally. I'll keep inputs modest on millet.

My education means I read the extension bulletins and I use improved seed for wheat and hybrid for maize without hesitation. For squash I go improved varieties that I know from experience yield well in this county's sandy loam.
